answer: A mechanism that actually bites: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because echo only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, dune is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any ferrous approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
